messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for POST /v1/generate across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Error rate ~6.8% at 2026-03-14T08:41:00Z. Paging on-call.

sara: picking up the page. dashboards show 502/504 + connection timeouts, tail latency spiking >5s.

alex: I'm seeing a flood of KV eviction logs and some checksum warnings from runtime. could be cache-layer related.

leo: which pool? any recent rollouts? I pushed a prefix-cache micro-optimization to canary last night.

priya: support noise: 9 customers reporting timeouts in the last 10m, 3 escalations. preparing customer update.

alex: pulling runtime excerpt now:
```
2026-03-14T08:39:58Z runtime INFO kv_cache evict_count=14230 evict_rate=620/s checksum_failures=137 corrupted_entries=63
2026-03-14T08:40:01Z runtime WARN prefix_cache lookup_miss=12045 hit=430 eviction_burst=true
2026-03-14T08:40:02Z gateway ERROR downstream_timeout target=10.4.7.23 service=kv-shard
```

sara: checksum_failures + corrupted_entries suggest serving bad cache entries -> worker errors and 502s.

emily: can we toggle the prefix cache flag remotely? fallback to read-through should reduce corrupted hits.

leo: yes, control plane supports runtime flags. proposal: flip prefix_cache.enabled=false on canary, monitor for 15m, then roll to region pools if stable. also schedule targeted purge of corrupted keys.

alex: mitigation steps I recommend: 1) disable prefix cache on canary 2) run safe purge on affected shards 3) temporarily limit noncritical customer concurrency 4) add a per-shard checksum spike alert.

ops-bot: control-plane change accepted for pool=canary. applied: prefix_cache.enabled=false. no restart required.

priya: customer message (sent): "We're investigating an intermittent increase in 502/504 responses affecting some generate requests. We've rolled back a cache optimization in affected clusters and are monitoring the recovery. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." :white_check_mark:

alex: canary error rate dropped to ~1.9% at 08:47 UTC after flag flip. eu-west still at ~3.6%.

leo: starting purge job for suspected corrupted keys on shard 7/12 during low traffic window. dry-run found ~1,120 suspicious keys.

ops-bot: purge job started: python tools/purge_kv.py --shard 7 --confirm --batch=500. tracking id purge-176861-7.

alex: purge deleted 1,108 keys from shard 7; checksum_failures on that shard now down to 2, corrupted_entries=0. CPU spike noted but within SLO.

sara: great. roll flag off for eu-west pool next if metrics keep improving. We have a handoff at 09:15 UTC; I'll hand to alex for 09:15-11:00 window.

priya: support ticket log updated with affected customers and incident reference INC-176861. will prepare follow-up email after RCA.

leo: follow-ups for postmortem: identify root cause in prefix-cache path (race condition in write path?), add automated rollback trigger when checksum_failures > X/min, add canary isolation test for cache corruption, and surface corrupted_entry metric per-shard to dashboards.

emily: also test safe-read fallback so that if a prefix lookup checksum fails we fetch from KV rather than serve. that could be an autoswitch in runtime.

alex: handoff note: I'm primary on-call until 11:00 UTC. monitoring hooks: grafana alert group 'generate-5xx', runtime 'kv.checksum_failures', purge job tracker purge-176861-7. ping me directly for any regression.

incident-bot: status update: mitigation applied -> partial recovery. incident state: active -> mitigation in progress. next update scheduled in 15m.

sara: closing urgent comms loop for now. we'll run RCA and schedule a postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-ml. thanks everyone for the rapid rollback and purge. :heart:
